newsitem.title: USA: Genesis teams with investors to acquire Multicare.
newsitem.headline: Genesis teams with investors to acquire Multicare.

text.p: Genesis Health Ventures Inc. said Monday it is teaming with two investment companies to acquire Multicare Cos. Inc., a New Jersey-based long-term health care company, for $1.4 billion.

Genesis, a Kennett Square, Pa.-based company which provides care for the elderly, said it will team with investment companies Cypress Group LLC and Texas Pacific Group to form ElderCare Acquisition Corp. and begin a tender offer for Multicare shares at $28 a share.
Multicare stock rose $1.25 to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in consolidated late afternoon trading. Genesis stock rose 12.5 cents to at $35.25, also on the NYSE.

Multicare, which had first-quarter 1997 annualized revenues of about $675 million, operates 155 facilities with about 16,000 beds. The company has about 37.0 million fully diluted shares and $342 million in debt outstanding, excluding $75 million in convertible debt.
Genesis will invest $300 million in exchange for about 42 percent of the new acquisition venture and Cypress and Texas Pacific will invest $420 million for the remaining 58 percent.

Under an agreement, Genesis will have the option to acquire the equity of the new company from Cypress and Texas Pacific after four years, and Cypress and Texas will have the option to sell their equity of the new company to Genesis after five years.
Genesis Chief Executive Officer Michael Walker said the company anticipates $19 million in cost savings from the Multicare acquisition.

In a telephone conference call with reporters, Walker also said the transaction is expected to have a neutral impact on earnings in the first 12 months, but added that earnings "will increase substantively later on."

Although Walker said the deal will make Genesis Health the third largest U.S. company based on beds served, he stressed that the company concentrates on providing services to keep the elderly out of nursing homes.
"Our goal is to help these individuals maintain their health and independence ... rather than being institutionalized," he said.
"The long-term care industry is outmoded and outdated," he said.

The transaction will expand Genesis's presence in regions already served, such as New England, as well as create a presence in West Virginia, western Pennsylvania and eastern Ohio. Walker said little overlap will occur by uniting the two companies.
Walker also said Genesis does not intend to focus on acquisitions after this transaction.
"We need to develop our infrastructure and our ability to market ourselves to the managed care organizations of the world," he said.
The agreement, which was approved by the boards of directors of both Genesis and MultiCare, is anticipated to close in the third quarter.
